meta.routePrinciple: Coastal-access-balanced planning line: stay nearer the extraction coast where practical, move outward only to clear headland/shoal/tidal sectors, then take the shortest useful water chord.

goNoGo.rule: Recheck Met Éireann marine warnings and Sea Area Forecast at Friday and event-day gates.
Reliable visual control of paddlers and support craft is required.
Carlston / skipper signs off actual wind, gusts and direction; ordinary drift/time cost is an operational constraint until control or recovery margin is threatened.

goNoGo.item: Mandatory exits / land extraction chain usable
goNoGo.rule: Verify Malin Beg, Teelin, Killybegs/Fintra, receiving coast and finish support before launch.
Current chart, tidal stream, swell, visibility and safety-boat access must support the chosen safe-water line.
No exposed leg without functioning safety-cover system.
VHF Channel 16 plus redundant emergency communications required.
Verify first aid, hypothermia equipment and event-carried AED plan.
Complete accountability and route/abort briefing before launch.

routeOptions.name: Malin Beg → coastal-access corridor → Muckross offing → Bullockmore West Cardinal → Bundoran
routeOptions.description: Stay comparatively close to the northern coast for extraction access, but step seaward around the exposed/headland sectors. After Bullockmore, take the efficient open-bay chord to the Bundoran outer approach. Actual offing remains a skipper/current-chart decision.

timeline: Carlston / Safety & Skipper Lead confirms GO/HOLD/NO-GO and selects the launch scenario.
Sign-on, equipment, VHF, safety craft, vehicles, float plan and land contact confirmed.
Route corridor, pods, signals, extraction points, emergency card and abort/escalation rules.
06:30, 07:45 or 09:00 scenario; start only with all hard checks resolved.
Deliberately conservative pace; prioritise rhythm, fueling, group integrity and easy extraction over early speed.
Use actual elapsed time, wind/VMG, group condition and remaining distance to reset the finish ETA and decide whether to continue, shorten or change receiving plan.
Carlston selects actual line using current chart/stream/sea; headcount and comms check.
Efficient receiving-coast chord; pod integrity, safety-boat cover and rolling position reports.
Confirm Boat Quay versus pre-verified alternate extraction.
All persons/craft accounted for; medical check, incident log, kit reconciliation and formal close.

roles.name: Carlston
roles.authority: Final on-water safety and navigation authority; approves launch, actual route/offing, continuation, diversion, casualty recovery and event termination.

roles.name: Barry Sweeney
roles.authority: Holds the float plan, roster/accountability state, launch/finish window, access/AED/extraction list and shore-side escalation chain; records major position/decision updates.

commandPrinciples: Carlston has final authority for on-water safety/navigation decisions.
Barry is the stable shore contact and should know the selected route, launch time, expected finish envelope and latest major position.
The sporting/fundraising objective is suspended during any serious incident until accountability and safety are restored.
Mobile numbers remain crew-only/manual fields; public site names the roles but does not publish private numbers.
preLaunch: Confirm roster/headcount, pods/buddies and any private medical information held by the designated crew lead.
Confirm safety craft fuel/mechanics, recovery space, tow/recovery equipment, chart/plotter and VHF.
Test primary and backup VHF; confirm Channel 16 distress capability and internal working channel/callsign if assigned.
Confirm event-carried AED, first aid, hypothermia/dry kit, spare paddle/board and repair kit.
Confirm launch, Teelin, Killybegs/Fintra, receiving-coast and finish extraction arrangements and drivers.
Barry receives float plan, selected launch scenario, expected 7–10 h finish envelope and emergency contact chain.
normalOps: Paddlers remain in assigned pod/buddy structure; lead controls pace and sweep confirms the tail.
First ~25 km is intentionally slow/cruisy. Fuel/hydrate by elapsed time; technique or cognition decline is a decision signal.
Headcount/visual check at major route gates and after any stop, recovery, equipment issue or course change.
Safety craft maintains a predictable support position that preserves rapid recovery without forcing paddlers into a poor line.
Barry receives position/decision updates at agreed gates and whenever route, ETA or extraction plan materially changes.

incidentStates.meaning: Operational constraint or minor incident increasing time/workload.
incidentStates.action: Close group, reassess ETA/extraction and resolve before it compounds.

incidentStates.meaning: Control/recovery margin lost, serious injury/illness, missing person, severe visibility/comms issue, safety-boat failure or other life-safety concern.
incidentStates.action: Sporting objective suspended; activate emergency response/Coast Guard as indicated.

procedures.title: Separated paddler / person in water
procedures.steps: Call STOP; maintain visual; safety craft/competent rescuer recovers; headcount and exposure/injury assessment. If visual is lost, drift is rapid or recovery is uncertain, activate Coast Guard immediately.

procedures.title: Casualty recovery / transfer
procedures.steps: Stabilise flotation and airway/breathing/circulation; recover to safety craft where safe; protect from cold; select nearest suitable transfer/extraction with Coast Guard guidance when required.

procedures.title: Serious medical incident
procedures.steps: Immediate 112/999 Coast Guard or VHF Ch16 for life threat, reduced consciousness, breathing problem, drowning, major bleeding, severe hypothermia, chest pain or other serious concern. Give exact position and emergency-card information.

procedures.title: Immersion / hypothermia
procedures.steps: Rapid controlled recovery; remove/protect from further exposure; dry/insulate; monitor consciousness/breathing; escalate for significant cold injury or deterioration.

procedures.title: Board / paddle / leash failure
procedures.steps: Keep paddler with flotation; deploy spare/transfer/tow/recover. If controlled progression cannot be restored promptly, extract or abort.

procedures.title: Safety-boat failure
procedures.steps: Stop exposed progression; regroup; use backup comms; move only toward the safest feasible extraction/holding plan. Do not continue the exposed objective without adequate safety cover.

procedures.title: Reduced visibility / group-control loss
procedures.steps: Close formation, reduce speed, establish positive accounting and position. If reliable visual/control cannot be maintained, abort/hold and seek Coast Guard assistance when necessary.

procedures.title: Collision / marine traffic
procedures.steps: Avoid traffic early; skipper controls crossing/avoidance. Following collision or injury, account for all people/craft, assess damage/medical needs and escalate appropriately.

procedures.title: Lost emergency comms
procedures.steps: Switch to backup VHF/phone/beacon; regroup and shorten. No exposed leg without a reliable emergency communications path.

procedures.title: Route shortening / extraction
procedures.steps: Carlston selects the safest practical water/landing plan; Barry mobilises land vehicle/contact chain; confirm all persons/craft accounted for at transfer.

procedures.title: Event termination
procedures.steps: Carlston declares termination; Barry records it and coordinates shore response. No demobilisation until every person/craft is accounted for and incidents are logged.

safetyHazards.hazard: Group separation / loss of visual control
safetyHazards.control: Pod/buddy structure, sweep, safety craft, headcounts; stop progression immediately if anyone is unaccounted for.
First aid/AED/hypothermia capability, rapid safety-craft recovery and early Coast Guard activation for life threats.
PFD/BA, thermal system, rapid recovery, dry/hypothermia kit and monitoring.

safetyHazards.hazard: Fatigue severe enough to degrade safe capability
safetyHazards.control: Cruisy early pace, scheduled fueling/hydration, technique/cognition checks and early extraction before deterioration.
Spare paddle/board, recovery/tow capability and safety-boat cover.
Pre-launch mechanical/fuel check, redundancy and no exposed continuation without adequate cover.
Skipper lookout/avoidance, compact group and traffic-aware crossing decisions.

safetyHazards.hazard: Visibility loss severe enough to lose group/escort control
safetyHazards.control: Close formation; no exposed progression when positive visual/accountability cannot be maintained.
No-go/abort when thunderstorms threaten the operating window.

safetyHazards.hazard: Loss of emergency communications / accurate position reporting
safetyHazards.control: Redundant VHF, phone/beacon backups, GPS position card and no exposed leg without emergency comms.
Coastal-access-balanced northern route, verified exits, land contact/vehicles and safety-craft recovery plan.

operationalConstraints.response: Do not aim for the apex. Hold enough offing to stay outside the troublesome close-in/shallow-water sector, then resume the shortest useful chord.
Primarily increases paddling line and can make safety-boat access awkward. Give extra sea room where recovery access would otherwise be poor.

operationalConstraints.constraint: Bullockmore / St John's shoals, rocks and cardinal geometry
operationalConstraints.response: Use Bullockmore/current chart as the shared control; route cost is normally extra distance/line selection, escalating only if control/recovery margin is compromised.
Ordinarily treat as slower VMG/drift-correction and revised ETA. Escalate to a safety hazard if group control or reliable recovery can no longer be maintained.
Closer coastal route between headlands; step outward only through the headland influence, then return to useful extraction proximity.
Verify selected extraction window and vehicle/boat access before relying on it.
Coordinate Boat Quay reception and retain a verified alternate receiving/extraction option.
Minor while routine. It becomes a safety issue only where a casualty could not be recovered/transferred with acceptable delay.

escalationPrinciple: An operational constraint becomes a safety hazard when its magnitude or context removes group control, reliable recovery, emergency communications, adequate safety-boat access or another required safety margin.

aedMap.legend: Red markers indicate public-access AEDs; amber markers indicate internal/opening-hours access. Re-verify event-day availability.
aedMap.eventRule: Carry a checked event AED where practicable; do not depend solely on an unverified public cabinet.

Road access exists near the lighthouse/headland; do not assume it is a safe water landing without local confirmation.
Verify water depth/pier access if Route B is selected.
AED reported at lifeguard station during lifeguard hours; verify coverage on event day.
Finish command-post candidate; emergency activation remains Coast Guard via 112/999 or VHF Ch16.
